name: Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Deva Gosvāmī

fields.aka: Śrīla Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Deva Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Bhakti Rakṣak Śrīdhar Dev-Gosvāmī
fields.appearance: Kārtika Kṛṣṇa Navamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 1895, at Hapaniya (Burdwan)
fields.disappearance: Śrāvaṇa Amāvasyā (Gauḍīya calendar); 12 August 1988, at Navadvīpa
fields.place: Born at Hapaniya, Burdwan district (West Bengal); Calcutta; founded the Śrī Caitanya Sārasvata Maṭha in Navadvīpa (samādhi)
fields.disciples: Bhakti Sundara Govinda Mahārāja (his successor); gave sannyāsa to Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava (Katwa) and Bhakti Sāraṅga Gosvāmī
fields.notes: Born in a brāhmaṇa family of the Bhaṭṭācārya order; studied at Baharampur. Joined the Gauḍīya Maṭha in 1926. Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī named him 'Bhakti Rakṣaka' (guardian of devotion) and 'Śrīdhara', praised his Bhaktivinoda-viraha-daśakam and asked him to sing Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī-pada just before his departure. Revered as the senior of the line after 1937; lifelong friend of A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī, who gave him part of his Calcutta house. Preached in Bengali, Hindi, Sanskrit and English.

name: Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja

fields.aka: Vinodabihārī Brahmacārī, Kṛtiratna Prabhu, Bhīma (birth name), Śailendranātha Guhaṭhākurtā, Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja, Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.appearance: Māgha Kṛṣṇa Tṛtīyā (= Phālguna Kṛṣṇa Tṛtīyā in the Gauḍīya calendar); 24 January 1898, at Banaripara (Barisal)
fields.disappearance: Āśvina Pūrṇimā, Śāradīya Rāsa Pūrṇimā (Gauḍīya calendar); 6 October 1968, 6.15 pm, at the Devānanda Gauḍīya Maṭha, Navadvīpa
fields.place: Born at Banaripara (Barisal district, East Bengal); Daulatpur College; Māyāpura (dīkṣā at the Yogapīṭha); Allahabad; Calcutta (Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti, 1940); Katwa (sannyāsa); Devānanda Gauḍīya Maṭha, Navadvīpa (samādhi); Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha, Mathurā; Chinsurah; Medinīpura
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī (harināma at 16; dīkṣā on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1919 at the Yogapīṭha, Māyāpura); sannyāsa on Bhādra Pūrṇimā at Katwa from Bhakti Rakṣaka Śrīdhara Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Trivikrama Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja; gave sannyāsa to A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda (Mathurā, 17 September 1959)
fields.notes: Father: Śaratcandra Guhaṭhākurtā; mother: Bhuvanamohinī Devī (landholder family); youngest of four brothers, one of them Bhakti Kevala Auḍulomi Mahārāja. Called 'Vinoda' and a 'Vedāntic paṇḍita' by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī, who said «Vinoda will see to it»; the first to receive the guru-mantra. Blessed by Gaura Kiśora dāsa Bābājī. Founded the Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti with Abhaya Caraṇa (Bhaktivedānta Svāmī) and Nṛsiṁhānanda Brahmacārī (Akṣaya Tṛtīyā 1940). Edited the Gauḍīya Patrikā. Sannyāsa day: Bhādra Pūrṇimā.

fields.aka: Heramba Kumāra Bandyopādhyāya (birth name), Hayagrīva dāsa Brahmacārī, Bhakti Dayita Mādhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja, B.D. Mādhava Mahārāja
fields.appearance: Kārtika Śukla Ekādaśī, Utthāna Ekādaśī (Gauḍīya calendar); Friday 18 November 1904, 8 am, at Kanchanpara (Faridpur)
fields.place: Born at Kanchanpara (Madaripur, Faridpur district, East Bengal, on the Padmā); Haridvāra and the Himalayas; Calcutta; Assam (Tezpur, Guwahati, Goalpara, Sorbhog); Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha, Purī (sannyāsa); founded the Śrī Caitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha and more than 20 maṭhas all over India
fields.guru: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura (harināma and dīkṣā in 1927 at the Ultadanga Gauḍīya Maṭha, Calcutta); sannyāsa on Gaura Pūrṇimā 1944 at Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha, Purī, from Bhakti Gaurava Vaikhānasa Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Bhakti Vallabha Tīrtha Mahārāja (his successor); gave sannyāsa to 21 disciples (1965-1977)
fields.notes: Father: Niśikānta Deva Śarmā Bandyopādhyāya (died when he was 4); mother: Śaivalinī Devī. Learned the whole Bhagavad-gītā by heart at 11. Searched for God in the Himalayas; met his guru in Māyāpura in 1925. Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī said he had 'volcanic energy' and wanted to send him to the West. Founded the Śrī Caitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha (registered 1953).

fields.aka: Hrydaya Bon Maharaja, Bhakti Hridoy Bon, Śrīla Bhakti Hṛdaya Vana Mahārāja, Bhakti Hṛdaya Vana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Narendranātha Mukherjī (birth name), Nandasuno Brahmacārī
fields.appearance: Caitra Śukla Pañcamī (Gauḍīya calendar); 1901, in East Bengal
fields.disappearance: Śrāvaṇa Kṛṣṇa Dvitīyā (Gauḍīya calendar); 7 July 1982, 9.04 pm, at Vṛndāvana
fields.place: Born in East Bengal; England and Germany (1930s); Vārāṇasī (1941); the Himalayas; bhajana-kuṭīra and samādhi at the Madana-mohana Ghera, Vṛndāvana; Institute of Oriental Philosophy, Vṛndāvana; Nandagrāma (school, Sanātana Gosvāmī's bhajana-kuṭīra); Śrī Caitanya Maṭha, Māyāpura
fields.guru: Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura (dīkṣā 1918; sannyāsa 1924, the third to receive it from him); bābājī veśa from Advaita dāsa Bābājī of Govardhana
fields.disciples: Many thousands of disciples; sannyāsīs: Kṛṣṇānanda, Rasānanda, Rasikānanda, Mohanānanda, Sudhānanda, Śyāmānanda, Mādhavānanda, Gopānanda, Keśavānanda and Śatānanda Bon Mahārāja; Sadānanda (Dr E. G. Schulze); śikṣā-guru of Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja
fields.works: Translation of Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu, The Gītā as a Chaitanyite Reads It, Śrī Caitanya, Viraha-vedanā, Vaikuṇṭher Pathe (On the Way to Vaikuṇṭha) and other books in German, English, Hindi and Bengali
fields.notes: Father: Brahmarṣi Rajanīkānta, a Vedic scholar and devotee. Lifelong celibate. One of the leading preachers of the Gauḍīya Maṭha; first to preach in Europe and to bring Western devotees to India. After his guru's departure did years of austerity (Vārāṇasī, the Himalayas, an underground cell in Vṛndāvana 1943-46). Founded the Institute of Oriental Philosophy and the Rādhā-Govinda Trust; built a primary school in Nandagrāma. Late in life ācārya of the Śrī Caitanya Maṭha (Māyāpura).

fields.name: Bhakti Vaibhava Purī Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Vaibhava Purī Gosvāmī Mahārāja, B.V. Purī Mahārāja, Nṛsiṁha Kavirāja, Nṛsiṁhānanda Prabhu
fields.appearance: Māgha Kṛṣṇa Ṣaṣṭhī (Gauḍīya calendar); 1913, at Fulta near Berhampur (Ganjam, Orissa)
fields.disappearance: Phālguna Śukla Saptamī (Gauḍīya calendar); samādhi at Purī
fields.place: Born at Fulta (Ganjam, Orissa); Berhampur; Bhanjanagar; Māyāpura; Kovvur and Madras (1937-42, 1948-66); Kakinada (1966); Visakhapatnam; Rajahmundry; Purī (Śrī Caitanya Candra Āśrama, Iṭoṭā); Sevā-kuñja, Vṛndāvana
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda (initiation on 3 August 1936 at Māyāpura); dīkṣā from Ananta Vāsudeva, whom he later left; sannyāsa on 7 February 1966 at Māyāpura from Bhakti Svarūpa Giri Mahārāja
fields.works: Chief editor of the monthly The Siddhānta; books in Telugu, Oriyā, Hindi and English (Śrī Bhakti Vijñāna Nityānanda Book Trust, 1988)
fields.notes: Parents: Śrī Dāmodara and Śrīmatī Devī; the second of four sons, named Nṛsiṁha. B.A. from Khallikote College; freedom fighter; Āyurvedic doctor (pupil of Kavirāja Madhusūdana Śarmā). Founder-ācārya of the Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mission (Kakinada 1966, Purī 1983; 18 maṭhas). Founding member of the WVA. Intimate friend of A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī (Rajahmundry 1971, Visakhapatnam 1973).

fields.name: Bhakti Vicāra Yāyāvara Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Vichar Yajavara, Bhakti Vichar Yayabar Mahārāj, Jajabar Mahārāj, Yāyāvara Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Gave sannyāsa to Bhakti Kumuda Santa Mahārāja (Remuṇā, 12 February 1942)
fields.notes: Disciple of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda. His Vaiṣṇava mission has seven temples. He was the first to proclaim that Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja was an empowered incarnation (śaktyāveśa-avatāra) of the Lord; later Śrīla B.R. Śrīdhara Mahārāja said the same. A good kīrtana singer.

fields.aka: A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda, Abhaya Caraṇa De (birth name), Abhaya Caraṇāravinda, Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja, Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja Prabhupāda
fields.appearance: Bhādra Kṛṣṇa Navamī, Nandotsava (Gauḍīya calendar); 1896, Calcutta
fields.disappearance: Kārtika Śukla Caturthī (Gauḍīya calendar); 14 November 1977, Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma Mandir, Vṛndāvana
fields.place: Born in Calcutta; Allahabad (Prayāga); Bombay; Jhansi; Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha, Mathurā (sannyāsa 1959); Rādhā-Dāmodara temple, Vṛndāvana; Delhi; New York (26 Second Avenue, ISKCON 1966); Māyāpura; samādhi at the Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma Mandir, Vṛndāvana
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Mahārāja (harināma and dīkṣā at Prayāga, 1932); sannyāsa on 17 September 1959 at Mathurā from Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.disciples: More than 5,000 initiated disciples; among them Gour Govinda Mahārāja
fields.works: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta (17 volumes), Nectar of Devotion, Kṛṣṇa and some 60 large volumes in all; the magazine Back to Godhead (1944)
fields.notes: Father: Gour Mohan De; mother: Rajanī. Met Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī in 1922, who told him to preach in English in the West. Co-founder of the Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti (1940). Founder-ācārya of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (New York, July 1966), the Bhaktivedānta Book Trust and the Bhaktivedānta Institute. Sannyāsa day: Bhādra Pūrṇimā (Viśvarūpa-mahotsava).

fields.name: Bhakti Kumuda Santa Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Kumud Santa Mahārāja, Bhakti Kumud Santa Gosvāmī, Rādhāramaṇa dāsa, Rāga-kumuda
fields.appearance: Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Ṣaṣṭhī (Gauḍīya calendar); 2 Vaiśākha 1921, at Narma (Medinīpura)
fields.place: Born at Narma (Medinīpura, West Bengal); Calcutta; Māyāpura; Prapanna Āśrama (Brahmanpara, Howrah); Burma (1936); Remuṇā (sannyāsa); Śrī Gaurāṅga Maṭha, Keshiary; Śrī Caitanya Āśramas at Kharagpur, Behala (Calcutta) and Purī; Chhekati
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (harināma as a student; saffron cloth on 20 March 1930); sannyāsa on 12 February 1942 at Remuṇā from Bhakti Vicāra Yāyāvara Mahārāja; śikṣā from Bhakti Hṛdaya Bon Mahārāja
fields.works: Guru-dāsatva hoy mor paricaya; Saṁlāpe Śikṣā; Patre Upadeśa; Gītā-siddhānta-sāra; Santa-vāṇī; Śrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhur Jīvanī; Sādhana-kaṇa; Dāmodara-vrata-māhātmya; Bhakti-gīti; Dīkṣā; Bengali translations of Moha-mudgara and Moha-kuṭhāra
fields.notes: Born in the house of Śrī Vaikuṇṭhanātha Rāya (astrologer, doctor and landlord); mother Śrīmatī Ratnamayī Devī; youngest of three sons. Joined Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī at eleven; his guru gave him the title 'Rāga-kumuda'. Preached in India and Burma, led the Navadvīpa parikramā with Bhakti Vilāsa Tīrtha Mahārāja, and from 1975 in Europe.

fields.name: Bhakti Prapanna Dāmodara Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.aka: Bhakti Prappan Dāmodar, Bhaktiprappan Dāmodar Gosvāmī, Ek-khodhi (childhood name), Cidānanda dāsa Brahmacārī
fields.disappearance: Guru Pūrṇimā, Monday 14 July 2003, at brāhma-muhūrta, in Purī (Śrī Śrī Jagannātha Caitanya Saṅgha); cremated by the sea
fields.place: Born at Maheshpur (Jessore district, now Bangladesh); Gauḍīya Maṭha, Ultadanga, Calcutta (from 1921); Jhargram; Vṛndāvana (sannyāsa); Puruṣottama Maṭha, Purī; Māyāpura; Śrī Śrī Jagannātha Caitanya Saṅgha, Gaur Bhat Sahi Road, Purī
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura (dīkṣā in 1932); sannyāsa in May 1947 at Vṛndāvana from Bhakti Sāraṅga Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Lalitā Mādhava dāsa, Sudevī dāsī, Prāṇa Govinda dāsa, Kṛṣṇa Kāntā dāsī, Deva Prasāda dāsa, Aniruddha dāsa
fields.notes: Given to Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī by his father at the age of six (1921) and lived with him from then on. Learned astrology from his guru; B.A. Received the small Māyāpura maṭha of Bhakti Vijñāna Āśrama Mahārāja; helped ISKCON obtain land and gave his maṭha for the Bhaktivedānta Book Trust building; published the proof of Mahāprabhu's birthplace. From the early 1980s lived in Purī, worshipping Śrī Śrī Gaura-Gadādhara and Mahābhāva-Rasarāja.

fields.appearance: Māgha Kṛṣṇa Dvādaśī (Gauḍīya calendar); in Burdwan district, near Ambikā-Kālnā
fields.disappearance: Kārtika Śukla Tṛtīyā (Gauḍīya calendar); 7 November 2002, 12.25 pm, in Navadvīpa-dhāma (Māyāpura)
fields.place: Born in Burdwan district, near Ambikā-Kālnā; Chinsurah; Navadvīpa (Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti)
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.disciples: Śikṣā-guru of Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja
fields.notes: Joined the Gauḍīya Maṭha by the preaching of Narottamānanda Brahmacārī (Bhakti Kamala Madhusūdana Mahārāja). One of the three pillars of the Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti with Vāmana and Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja; in charge of its preaching and parikramās. Outspoken and very humble; did the Govardhana parikramā barefoot for a month after 75.

fields.aka: Sri-rupa Siddhanti Gosvami Maharaja, Srirupa Siddhanti Gosvāmī Mahārāja, Siddhasvarūpa Brahmacārī, Bhakti Śrīrūpa Siddhāntī Gosvāmī
fields.place: Gauḍīya Sārasvata Āśrama, Satasan Road, Jagannātha Purī
fields.guru: Śrīla Bhakti Siddhānta Sarasvatī; śikṣā from Bhakti Viveka Bhāratī Mahārāja and from Vinodabihārī Brahmacārī (Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava)
fields.works: Bengali translation of Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa's Govinda-bhāṣya; commentaries on the twelve principal Upaniṣads; translations of the Gītā commentaries of Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa and Viśvanātha Cakravartī; Guru-preṣṭha
fields.notes: As Siddhasvarūpa Brahmacārī he refuted the followers of Vivekānanda in public, to his guru's delight. Co-founder with Bhakti Viveka Bhāratī Mahārāja of the Śrī Sārasvata Gauḍīya Āśrama and Mission (three branches); built three temples with sculpted theistic exhibitions. Led the funeral rites of Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Mahārāja (1968).
Disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; founding member of the WVA (World Vaiṣṇava Association).
Disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; founding member of the WVA (World Vaiṣṇava Association).

Direct disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; honorary member of the WVA. Very humble, he refuses any honour; travels between Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Purī glorifying the Lord, and teaches the glories of Rādhā-kuṇḍa and the need for strict sādhana.
Disciple of Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī; founding member of the WVA (World Vaiṣṇava Association).
